topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and sets the scope for the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and damage recognition by pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms and receptor pathways used by the innate immune system to detect conserved microbial patterns and cellular damage.

topics.label: Acute inflammatory signaling, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells initiate local and systemic inflammatory responses, mediate leukocyte extravasation into tissues, and can cause septic shock when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is terminated through passive and active mechanisms, and how unresolved damage leads to tissue repair, chronic inflammation, or granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing for the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on complement.
